rules.summary: The provider must accept the OVS exam fee as payment in full and may not bill the survivor for the forensic exam services.
rules.quote: The hospital, sexual assault examiner program, or licensed health care provider must accept this fee as payment in full for these specified services. No additional billing of the survivor for said services is permissible.

rules.summary: Private insurance can be used for the exam only if the survivor chooses to assign it, and then the survivor owes no deductible, coinsurance, or balance bill.
rules.quote: A sexual assault survivor may voluntarily assign any private insurance benefits to which they are entitled for the healthcare forensic examination, in which case the hospital or healthcare provider may not charge the office; provided, however, in the event the sexual assault survivor assigns any private health insurance benefit, such coverage shall not be subject to annual deductibles or coinsurance or balance billing by the hospital, sexual assault examiner program or licensed health care provider.

rules.summary: Hospitals must make sure survivors are not billed for forensic exams and must tell them, orally and in writing, they can decline to give insurance information and have OVS pay instead.
rules.quote: ensuring sexual assault survivors are not billed for sexual assault forensic exams and are notified orally and in writing of the option to decline to provide private health insurance information and have the office of victim services reimburse the hospital for the exam

rules.summary: A provider that accepts OVS payment for the exam takes it as payment in full and may not bill the survivor for the difference between its charges and what OVS paid.
rules.quote: The billing provider may not bill victims/survivors or their guardians for the difference between charged amounts and the amount reimbursed by OVS.
rules.pinpoint: OVS FRE Provider Billing Manual (March 2026), III.c Reimbursement Rates

params.payer: New York State Office of Victim Services (direct reimbursement to the provider)

rules.summary: The hospital or provider gives sexual assault survivors exam services free of charge and bills the Office of Victim Services directly.
rules.quote: such hospital, sexual assault examiner program, or licensed healthcare provider shall provide such services to the person without charge and shall bill the office directly.

params.payer: New York State Office of Victim Services

rules.summary: OVS pays the medical provider directly for the exam when the survivor has no private insurance or chooses not to use it.
rules.quote: OVS can directly reimburse medical providers for forensic rape exams when sexual assault survivors do not have private health insurance or choose not to use their insurance.
rules.pinpoint: OVS Forensic Rape Exam Direct Reimbursement Program page

params.payer: OVS pays only for exam-related services; unrelated care goes to insurance first, then a compensation claim

rules.summary: OVS direct payment covers only services and medicines related to the forensic exam. Unrelated care in the same visit is not paid under the exam claim; it goes to the survivor's insurance first, then can be submitted to OVS as a regular compensation claim.
rules.quote: Only services and pharmaceuticals that are related to the forensic rape exam may be reimbursed under an FRE claim.
rules.pinpoint: OVS FRE Provider Billing Manual (March 2026), III Reimbursement

rules.summary: Out-of-pocket costs a sex offense victim (Penal Law article 130) incurs for a hospital or medical exam tied to the investigation or prosecution are covered.
rules.quote: an award shall include out-of-pocket expenses, including indebtedness reasonably incurred by the victim of a sex offense or the person responsible for the victim of such sex offense, as such sex offense is defined in article one hundred thirty of the penal law, for a hospital or medical examination in connection with the investigation or prosecution of any such offense.

rules.summary: Unreimbursed medical care and other necessary services caused by the injury count as out-of-pocket loss.
rules.quote: Out-of-pocket loss shall mean unreimbursed and unreimbursable expenses or indebtedness reasonably incurred for medical care or other services necessary as a result of the injury upon which such claim is based

rules.summary: Counseling is covered for physically injured crime victims and their spouse, children, or stepchildren (sex offense victims are presumed physically injured).
rules.quote: Such expenses or indebtedness shall include the cost of counseling for the eligible spouse, domestic partner, grandparents, parents, stepparents, guardians, brothers, sisters, stepbrothers, stepsisters, children, stepchildren or grandchildren of a homicide victim, and crime victims who have sustained a personal physical injury as the direct result of a crime and the spouse, children or stepchildren of such physically injured victim.

rules.summary: Reasonable travel to crime-related medical care is covered, with receipts for fares or the federal mileage rate for driving yourself.
rules.quote: medical expenses shall also include the reasonable transportation expenses incurred for necessary, causally related medical care which may include, but are not limited to, reasonable airplane, cab, bus or train fare, with receipts, or if a claimant has provided his or her own transportation, the federally recognized mileage reimbursement rate at the time the expense was incurred

rules.summary: Reasonable transportation to necessary court appearances in the prosecution is covered.
rules.quote: an award shall include reasonable transportation expenses incurred for necessary court appearances in connection with the prosecution of such crimes upon which the claim is based.

rules.summary: New or enhanced security devices can be covered when a physician, counselor, or the district attorney states the claimant's health is in imminent danger without the device.
rules.quote: In order for the costs associated with new or enhanced security devices, beyond those which, pursuant to the Executive Law are repaired or replaced under subdivision 2 of section 631, or are awarded under subdivision 12 of section 631 , to be compensable, the office shall require a statement from the claimant's physician or counselor, or the district attorney handling the victim's case, indicating that without the aid of such a device the claimant's health is in imminent danger.

rules.summary: Relocation costs are covered when moving is necessary for the victim's health or safety.
rules.quote: "Relocation expenses" shall mean the cost of relocating a crime victim, when relocation is necessary for the health or safety of the victim.

rules.summary: Lost earnings or support are capped at $30,000.
rules.quote: loss of earnings or support resulting from such injury not to exceed thirty thousand dollars

rules.summary: Lost earnings or support are paid at no more than $600 per week.
rules.quote: no such award shall exceed six hundred dollars for each week of lost earnings or support.

rules.summary: Relocation expenses are capped at $2,500.
rules.quote: reasonable relocation expenses not exceeding twenty-five hundred dollars

rules.summary: Employment-related transportation (extra cost of getting to work because of crime injuries) is capped at $2,500. Medical and court travel are not under this cap.
rules.quote: reasonable employment-related transportation expenses, not exceeding twenty-five hundred dollars

rules.summary: Crime scene cleanup and securing a crime scene (for example repairing doors, windows, and locks) are capped at $2,500.
rules.quote: the costs of crime scene cleanup and securing of a crime scene not exceeding twenty-five hundred dollars

rules.summary: Repair or replacement of essential personal property is capped at $2,500, with cash losses limited to $100.
rules.quote: Any award made for the cost of repair or replacement of essential personal property, including cash losses of essential personal property, shall be limited to an amount of twenty-five hundred dollars, except that all cash losses of essential personal property shall be limited to the amount of one hundred dollars.

params.item: items related to the victim's ability to communicate

rules.summary: Essential property related to the victim's ability to communicate is paid at the receipted amount, up to $1,500 per item.
rules.quote: All awards made pursuant to Executive Law article 22 and this Part related to a victim's ability to communicate shall be limited to the receipted amount, in an amount not exceeding one-thousand five-hundred dollars per item.

params.item: items for the safe operation of the victim's personal means of transportation

rules.summary: Essential property related to safely operating the victim's own means of transportation is paid at the receipted amount, up to $2,500 per item.
rules.quote: All awards made pursuant to Executive Law article 22 and this Part related to a victim's safe operation of their personal means of transportation shall be limited to the receipted amount, in an amount not exceeding two-thousand five-hundred dollars per item.

rules.summary: Medically necessary life-sustaining equipment lost or damaged in the crime has its own cap of $10,000 instead of the general essential property cap.
rules.quote: In the case of medically necessary life-sustaining equipment which was lost or damaged as the direct result of a crime, the award shall be limited to the amount of ten thousand dollars.

rules.summary: Outerwear, suits, and footwear are paid at the receipted amount, up to $500 per item.
rules.quote: Items of outerwear, suits and footwear shall be the receipted amount, in an amount not exceeding five-hundred dollars per item.

params.item: clothing other than outerwear, suits and footwear

rules.summary: Other clothing is paid at the receipted amount, up to $100 per item.
rules.quote: All other items of clothing shall be the receipted amount, in an amount not exceeding one-hundred dollars per item.

params.item: mattress and platform or box spring

rules.summary: A mattress and platform or box spring are paid at the receipted amount, up to $2,000.
rules.quote: Mattress and platform or box spring shall be the receipted amount, in an amount not exceeding two-thousand dollars.

params.item: bedding other than mattress and box spring

rules.summary: Other bedding is paid at the receipted amount, up to $500 in total.
rules.quote: All other items of bedding shall be the receipted amount, in a cumulative amount not exceeding five-hundred dollars.

rules.summary: Attorney fees for representation before OVS or on judicial review are capped at $1,000.
rules.quote: the cost of reasonable attorneys' fees for representation before the office and/or before the appellate division upon judicial review not to exceed one thousand dollars.

params.item: periodic monitoring or maintenance charges for security devices

rules.summary: For security devices, only the device and installation are covered; monitoring and maintenance fees are not.
rules.quote: Compensable costs shall be limited to the devices themselves and their installation, and shall not include the periodic service charges for monitoring or maintaining any such devices.

rules.summary: Meals during travel for medical care are not reimbursed as transportation.
rules.quote: Meals shall not be considered a related transportation expense.

params.item: purchase, lease or rental of a vehicle

rules.summary: Employment-related transportation does not cover buying, leasing, or renting a vehicle.
rules.quote: Such costs shall not include the purchase, lease or rental of a vehicle.

params.extension: Runs from the crime or its discovery; OVS may extend for good cause, and must extend if the claimant got no notice of the program and did not know they were eligible.

rules.summary: File within 3 years of the crime or its discovery; OVS may extend this for good cause.
rules.quote: A claim must be filed by the claimant not later than three years after the occurrence or discovery of the crime upon which such claim is based, three years after a court finds a lawsuit to be frivolous, or not later than three years after the death of the victim, provided, however, that upon good cause shown, the office may extend the time for filing.

params.extension: good reasons, including not knowing compensation existed or not knowing you may be eligible

rules.summary: Even after 3 years, OVS can waive the deadline for good reasons, such as not knowing the program existed or not knowing you were eligible.
rules.quote: Please keep in mind that even if it has been more than three years, OVS has the ability to waive this requirement if the claimant or victim/survivor can show they had good reasons for not filing a claim within that timeframe. Good reasons can include, but are not limited to not knowing that victim compensation existed, or not knowing that they may be eligible for compensation.
rules.pinpoint: OVS Compensation Program Updates for Victims and Survivors, Timely Filing

rules.summary: A police report is not required: the crime must have been reported, but records of a support agency for survivors of crime (such as a forensic exam facility or protective services agency) can show this instead of police records. No fixed reporting window appears in the statute.
rules.quote: the records of a support agency for survivors of crime or the records of a criminal justice agency show that such crime was reported.

rules.summary: A medical facility that provides forensic exams for rape and sexual assault counts as a support agency, so its records can stand in for a police report.
rules.quote: any medical facility established under the laws of the state that provides a forensic physical examination for victims of rape and sexual assault

rules.summary: For sex offenses, a family court also counts as a support agency.
rules.quote: in cases involving any sex offense or family offense a support agency for survivors of crime shall also include a family court

rules.summary: Since December 31, 2025, a victim service provider or a medical or mental health professional can fill out a Crime Verification Form instead of a police report.
rules.quote: Starting December 31, 2025, instead of filing a report with law enforcement, you can go to a local victim service provider , or a medical or mental health professional, and tell them that you or a loved one experienced a crime. The provider can fill out a short form to tell OVS about the crime.
rules.pinpoint: OVS Compensation Program Updates for Victims and Survivors, Reporting a Crime

rules.summary: Under the statute, when the victim cannot report to or cooperate with police because of age, physical or psychological state, cultural or language barriers, or another health or safety concern, a court that issued a restraining or protective order, a contracted victim services provider, or a licensed medical or mental health provider also counts as a support agency.
rules.quote: in cases where a physically injured claimant and/or victim is unable to report to or otherwise cooperate with a criminal justice agency because of the victim's age, physical condition, psychological state, cultural or linguistic barriers, or any other health or safety concern that jeopardizes the victim's wellbeing, a support agency for survivors of crime shall also include: (A) a court which issued a temporary or permanent restraining order or protective order against the party or parties alleged to have committed the crime against the victim, or (B) a "victim services provider"

rules.summary: Awards are reduced by payments from the offender, mandated insurance, public funds, the claimant's own insurance, and any emergency award.
rules.quote: Any award made pursuant to this article shall be reduced by the amount of any payments received or to be received by the claimant as a result of the injury (a) from or on behalf of the person who committed the crime, (b) under insurance programs mandated by law, (c) from public funds, (d) under any contract of insurance wherein the claimant is the insured or beneficiary, (e) as an emergency award pursuant to section six hundred thirty of this article.

rules.summary: OVS pays last: insurance or benefit plans must be billed first. The forensic exam is an exception (see the exam rules).
rules.quote: OVS is the payer of last resort and can only consider your out-of-pocket loss. OVS can only process payments for crime-related expenses. You must bill your insurance company or benefits plan before OVS can pay.

rules.summary: OVS considers whether the victim's own conduct contributed to the injury and can reduce or deny the award on that basis.
rules.quote: the office shall determine whether, because of such victim's conduct, the victim of such crime contributed to the infliction of such victim's injury, and the office shall reduce the amount of the award or reject the claim altogether, in accordance with such determination.

rules.summary: Being a victim of sexual assault is a mitigating factor, and OVS may then make the award with no conduct reduction.
rules.quote: However, when considering conduct contributing the office shall examine the following mitigating factors: the victim was a minor, a victim of human trafficking, a sex worker, or a victim of sexual assault. If any such mitigating factors are found in the investigation of the claim pursuant to subdivision (b) of section 525.5 of this part, the office may make an award without reduction for conduct contributing.

rules.summary: When an award is likely and waiting would cause undue hardship, OVS can make emergency awards totaling up to $2,500, which are later deducted from the final award.
rules.quote: the office may make one or more emergency awards to the claimant pending a final decision of the office or payment of an award in the case, provided, however, that the total amount of such emergency awards shall not exceed twenty-five hundred dollars.

rules.summary: Victims of sex offenses under Penal Law article 130 are presumed to have suffered physical injury, which is the usual gateway to compensation.
rules.quote: For the purposes of this subdivision, the victim of a sex offense as defined in article one hundred thirty of the penal law is presumed to have suffered physical injury.

params.rule: Crime committed in New York State

rules.summary: Acts committed in New York count as crimes for compensation whether or not anyone was arrested, charged, or prosecuted, and whether or not the claimant dealt with police.
rules.quote: an act committed in New York state which would, if committed by a mentally competent criminally responsible adult, who has no legal exemption or defense, constitute a crime as defined in and proscribed by law, regardless of whether any suspect was arrested, charged, apprehended or prosecuted for the commission of the act or whether the claimant has interacted with a criminal justice agency investigating such act

params.rule: New York residents victimized in a state without an eligible compensation program

rules.summary: A New York resident hurt by a crime in another state can apply only if that state has no eligible compensation program.
rules.quote: an act committed outside the state of New York against a resident of the state of New York which would be compensable had it occurred within the state of New York and which occurred in a state which does not have an eligible crime victim compensation program

params.target: NYS Office of Victim Services, AE Smith Building, 80 S. Swan Street, Albany, NY 12210-8002

rules.summary: A paper application and documents can be mailed to the OVS office in Albany.
rules.quote: Mailing Address: NYS Office of Victim Services AE Smith Building 80 S. Swan Street Albany, NY 12210-8002
rules.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 2, OVS Contact Information

rules.summary: The application and supporting documents can be emailed to the OVS intake address.
rules.quote: Email applications and documents to: OVSIntake@ovs.ny.gov
rules.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 2, OVS Contact Information

rules.summary: A claim can be filed online through the OVS Compass Applicant Portal, as a guest or with a NY.gov account.
rules.quote: Yes, you can visit https://ovs.ny.gov/ to access the secure OVS Compass Applicant Portal, or Victim Advocate Portal, and file an application online.
rules.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 1, FAQ: Is there another way to apply?

params.note: all bills and receipts for the crime-related goods and services claimed

rules.summary: Include all bills and receipts for the expenses described in the application.
rules.quote: All bills and receipts for expenses related to goods and services you described in this application.
rules.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 2, Processing Your Claim

params.note: the same instruction asks for all bills, not only receipts

rules.summary: Include the bills for the crime-related goods and services claimed.
rules.quote: All bills and receipts for expenses related to goods and services you described in this application.
rules.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 2, Processing Your Claim

params.note: HIPAA release form, one per medical or mental health provider; a blank copy is at the end of the application

rules.summary: Include one completed HIPAA authorization for each medical and mental health provider seen for crime-related care.
rules.quote: One completed HIPAA form for each medical and mental health provider you saw for services related to this crime.
rules.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 2, Processing Your Claim

params.note: letters from insurers or government agencies denying or approving payment

rules.summary: Include any letters from insurance companies or government agencies that denied or authorized payment for the claimed expenses.
rules.quote: Letters from any insurance or government agencies denying or authorizing payments related to goods and services you described in this application.
rules.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 2, Processing Your Claim

params.note: crime verification: one third-party document, such as a Crime Verification Form from a victim service provider or a medical or mental health professional

rules.summary: Only one third-party document confirming the crime is needed, and a Crime Verification Form from a victim service provider or medical or mental health professional works.
rules.quote: You only need to submit one document showing OVS that a third-party has confirmed that you or the victim/survivor experienced a crime. You can speak to a victim service provider or medical or mental health professional, and they can fill out a Crime Verification Form.
rules.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 9, Supporting Documentation for Crime Verification

params.note: optional; a police or other criminal justice agency report is one way to verify the crime, not the only way

rules.summary: A police or other criminal justice agency report can be submitted as the crime verification document, but it is a choice.
rules.quote: You may also choose to report the crime to law enforcement and submit a criminal justice agency report, like a police report, as part of this application.
rules.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 9, Supporting Documentation for Crime Verification

params.note: optional; the applicant can choose to use the forensic rape exam report as part of the application

rules.summary: If a forensic rape exam was done, the survivor can choose to use the exam report in the application.
rules.quote: If an FRE was performed, do you want to use the report as part of your application?
rules.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 10, Medical Care

params.note: Workers' Compensation or disability insurance decision letter, only if the victim has that coverage

rules.summary: If the victim has Workers' Compensation or disability insurance coverage, OVS needs that provider's decision letter.
rules.quote: If the victim has coverage through either Worker's Compensation or a Disability Insurance provider, OVS will need the decision letter from either Worker's Compensation or the Disability Insurance provider to help determine eligibility for compensation.
rules.pinpoint: OVS Victim Compensation Claim Application (Feb. 2026), page 16, Workers Compensation/Disability

params.agency: New York Department of State (Secretary of State)
params.enroll: You may apply online or by completing a pdf application. Completed applications may either be mailed or faxed. Filing instructions are on the form. (DOS ACP: (518) 474-7306, toll-free (855) 350-4595, Address Confidentiality Program, P.O. Box 1110, Albany, NY 12201-1110, fax (518) 474-0709.)

rules.summary: The Department of State runs an Address Confidentiality Program that gives eligible victims, including victims of a sexual offense, a designated substitute address to use instead of their real address, with free mail forwarding.
rules.quote: There is created in the office of the secretary of state a program to be known as the "address confidentiality program" to protect victims of domestic violence, victims of human trafficking, victims of kidnapping, victims of a sexual offense, victims of stalking, and reproductive health care services providers, employees, volunteers, patients, or immediate family members of reproductive health care services providers by authorizing the use of designated addresses for such victims and their minor children.

rules.summary: OVS records and proceedings on a victim's or claimant's compensation claim are confidential and are not shared with government or private entities, except for listed purposes such as criminal justice requests, judicial subpoenas, the claimant's own requests, and program administration.
rules.quote: Records maintained by the office and proceedings by the office based thereon regarding a claim submitted by a victim or a claimant shall be deemed confidential and shall not be shared with any government or private entity, with the following exceptions:

coverage.notes: total_cap: Article 22 sets no overall maximum award; it caps specific categories (lost earnings, relocation, property, etc.) and medical and counseling costs have no dollar cap in the statute. I did not record a total cap rather than infer one. Counseling rates: no per-session counseling fee cap was found in Executive Law 631 or in 9 NYCRR 525.3 or 525.12; 525.12(g)(4) lets OVS require proof that counseling is crime-related when a claim is filed more than one year after counseling began. minimum_loss: no minimum out-of-pocket loss requirement was found in the statute sections read. Security: covered for new or enhanced devices with a physician, counselor, or DA statement (525.12(g)(3)); no dollar cap found apart from the $2,500 crime scene securing cap. Financial difficulty: Exec. Law 631(6)(a) requires a finding of financial difficulty except for emergency awards and awards under ten thousand dollars (not a schema category). Reporting: the old one-week police reporting rule is no longer in Exec. Law 631(1); the current text accepts records of a support agency for survivors of crime. OVS pages say the Crime Verification Form is accepted only for claims filed on or after December 31, 2025. Reviewer additions: 9 NYCRR 525.12(h)(9) (LII text, last amended 2022) says direct-reimbursement exam expenses must relate to services within 120 hours of the incident, waived for a child victim or for good cause, and no kit reimbursement past 120 hours; the current Exec. Law 631(13) and the March 2026 OVS provider billing manual do not state this window, so it is not encoded as a rule. The per-item clothing, bedding, communication and transportation-item limits in 525.12(n)(1)-(4) do not apply when OVS finds the property is related to the victim's health or safety (525.12(n)(6)); the $2,500 statutory property cap still applies. The protective-order, victim services provider, and medical or mental health provider alternatives in Exec. Law 631(1)(c)(iii) are conditioned in the statute on the victim being unable to report to or cooperate with police for health or safety reasons; the OVS update page (NY-S7) describes the Crime Verification Form without that condition. processing_time: no saved OVS page, application, or statute section states a time for a decision or payment, so none is recorded.

researcher_notes: Statute text is from the NY Senate Open Legislation site (fetched via Chrome). 9 NYCRR text is from Cornell LII because the official Westlaw NYCRR site is script-heavy; LII shows the 525.12 amendment history through Oct 12, 2022, and its funeral cap ($6,000) is older than the current statute ($12,000 in Exec. Law 631(2)), so for any conflict the statute wins. Effective dates from OVS update pages: three-year filing deadline and Crime Verification Form alternative to police reports apply starting December 31, 2025; filing deadline previously shorter. Exec. Law 631(13)(b) also sets provider reimbursement ceilings for the exam ($800 / $1,200 / $2,500); these are provider rates, not survivor-facing, so I did not encode them. The OVS FRE page says claims received on or after February 3, 2026 are paid by a new OVS fee schedule. PHL 2805-i(1) has two versions of the no-billing paragraph (lettered (d) until May 9, 2027 and (g) after); the quoted text is identical in both. Expense caps with per='item' (clothing, communication items) are per-item limits from 9 NYCRR 525.12(n); per='item' is outside the schema's listed values but is what the regulation says. A phone would most plausibly fall under 'ability to communicate', but the regulation does not name phones. Essential personal property awards for adults generally require a physical injury; sex offense victims are presumed physically injured under Exec. Law 626(1). The older OVS FAQ page and 2022 guideline PDFs state superseded rules (one-week reporting, one-year filing, $500 property cap), so I did not use them. How to file: the English application link on the OVS page (ovs.ny.gov/compensation_application_english) still redirects to the Feb. 2026 fillable PDF saved as NY-S4 (552 AcroForm fields), so that is the newest version. Submission targets come from the application's contact section: mail to the Albany AE Smith Building address and email to OVSIntake@ovs.ny.gov; online filing is through OVS Compass (program.apply_url). The OVS page (NY-S1) also lists a Brooklyn office at 55 Hanson Place for the Compensation Division, but the application says to mail documents to the Albany address, so only Albany is encoded. No fax or in-person filing method is stated. The application also says documents can be sent later if not ready, and the OVS page says OVS may later ask for birth or death certificates, marriage licenses, insurance Explanations of Benefits, and receipts depending on the claim; those on-request items are not encoded as required documents. Photo ID, proof of residency, and wage verification are not requested up front; for lost wages the application says OVS contacts the employer. Address confidentiality: Exec. Law 108 (NY-S21) makes victims of a sexual offense (Penal Law article 130 and 255.25 to 255.27, including threats or attempts) eligible for the Department of State Address Confidentiality Program; applicants affirm they left their residence because of the acts and fear for their safety (108(2)(a)(i)), applications are filed with the office of the secretary (108(2)(c)), designated state, local or nonprofit agencies assist applicants (108(3)), and certification lasts four years (108(2)(e)). The DOS ACP pages (NY-S22, NY-S23) still describe eligibility as victims of domestic violence only and say participation is limited to New York State residents; the statute is broader and wins, so covers_sexual_assault is true from the statute. The enroll text and contact details come from the DOS apply page (NY-S23). Record confidentiality: Exec. Law 633(1) (NY-S20) exceptions are legitimate criminal justice requests (where the victim reported to a victim services provider instead of police, OVS may not share identifying information), judicial subpoenas, requests by the victim or claimant or their authorized representative, and purposes necessary for administering Article 22; 633(2) makes other OVS records (such as those under 631-a and 632-a) public; 633(3) keeps records that are confidential under other laws confidential.
